summary: A crag can both obstruct an approach and shelter someone who reaches it. David’s use of “my crag” in Psalm 18 takes its force from that experience.

senses.definition: Jonathan’s approach to the Philistines passes between two projecting crags. In the wilderness account water flows from the rock for the assembled people.
Samson stays in a cleft of the crag at Etam. David calls Yahweh his crag alongside his fortress and deliverer, using the shelter of terrain for the protection he has received.
After his victory over Edom in the Valley of Salt, Amaziah captures Sela and gives it the name Joktheel.

evidence.locator: Book I p. 1406, n20451, a crack or cleft in a mountain

note: Arabic silʿ designates a fissure in a mountain and offers a possible comparison. The locust term already belongs to the solam entry. The compound Sela-hammahlekoth already belongs to the chalaq entry.
